premise: On a windy day Archaeopteryx flaps until she's puffed and Glider can only glide down from a branch; Pteranodon spreads her wings and floats on the wind without a single flap, and shows them how to let it carry them.
inspiration: Aesop's 'The Eagle and the Jackdaw' turned kind: the big flyer doesn't show off; she shares the trick.
lesson: A friend who knows how shares it.
learning: Pteranodon could soar a long way on the wind, hardly flapping its wings.

en-US.title: Riding the Wind
en-US.text: {canvas:wind 0.6} {sfx:wind} [excited] Whoosh! It was a windy day in the valley. On a branch of the monkey-puzzle tree sat {archaeopteryx:enter} {archaeopteryx:go to branches} Archaeopteryx and {glider:enter} {glider:go to branches} Glider. {archaeopteryx:face happy} "Let's fly!" said Archaeopteryx. {archaeopteryx:live flap} She flapped and flapped, {archaeopteryx:go to rocks} all the way to the big flat rock… [sighs] and she was puffed out. {glider:live spread} Glider spread out his furry skin and {glider:go to meadow} glided… down, down, down into the ferns. {glider:face sad} "Gliding only goes down," he said. On the rock, {pteranodon:enter} {pteranodon:go to rocks} Pteranodon smiled. [warmly] "Watch." {pteranodon:go to sky right} She opened her wings wide and let the wind lift her. {pteranodon:live glide hold} Up she floated, round and round, {archaeopteryx:face surprised} and she didn't flap once. Not once! [in awe] "How?" asked Archaeopteryx. "Don't push against the wind," said Pteranodon. "Let it carry you." So Archaeopteryx held her wings out wide, {archaeopteryx:go to sky right} and up she went. {glider:face happy} Glider scampered {glider:go to branches by scurry} back up to his branch. Then {glider:go to sky right} he spread his skin, and the wind carried him too. [happily] {all:face happy} And there they floated, all three, with only one tiny flap between them. {archaeopteryx:wobble} Well… maybe two. {canvas:wind stop}

es-ES.title: A lomos del viento
es-ES.text: {canvas:wind 0.6} {sfx:wind} [excited] ¡Fiuuu! Hacía viento en el valle. En una rama de la araucaria estaban {archaeopteryx:enter} {archaeopteryx:go to branches} Arqueoptérix y {glider:enter} {glider:go to branches} Planeador. {archaeopteryx:face happy} —¡Vamos a volar! —dijo Arqueoptérix. {archaeopteryx:live flap} Aleteó y aleteó y aleteó {archaeopteryx:go to rocks} hasta la gran roca plana… [sighs] y llegó sin aliento. {glider:live spread} Planeador abrió su piel peludita y {glider:go to meadow} planeó… abajo, abajo, abajo, hasta el prado. {glider:face sad} —Planeando solo se va hacia abajo —dijo. En la roca, {pteranodon:enter} {pteranodon:go to rocks} Pteranodon sonrió. [warmly] —Mirad. {pteranodon:go to sky right} Abrió bien las alas y dejó que el viento la subiera. {pteranodon:live glide hold} Flotó hacia arriba, dando vueltas, {archaeopteryx:face surprised} y no aleteó ni una vez. ¡Ni una! [in awe] —¿Cómo lo haces? —preguntó Arqueoptérix. —No empujes contra el viento —dijo Pteranodon—. Deja que te lleve. Así que Arqueoptérix abrió las alas de par en par {archaeopteryx:go to sky right} y subió, subió. {glider:face happy} Planeador trepó corriendo {glider:go to branches by scurry} a su rama. Luego {glider:go to sky right} abrió la piel, y el viento lo llevó a él también. [happily] {all:face happy} Y allí flotaron los tres, con un solo aleteo entre todos. {archaeopteryx:wobble} Bueno… quizá dos. {canvas:wind stop}
